post.contentHtml:
H1 Operating Profit Up 62%: Why Did MARUWA Hit the Daily Limit?

MARUWA (5344) is a Japanese company listed on the Prime Market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange that makes ceramic substrates and electronic components. It announced its interim (first-half) results after the market closed on October 27, 2026. On the next trading day, its share price rose to ¥54,000, the maximum daily gain allowed ("limit-up"). This article looks at what we can read from these results and the market's reaction.

1. Key Points of the Interim Results

ItemH1 of FY ending March 2027YoY change
Net salesApprox. ¥46.9 billion+41.7%
Operating profitApprox. ¥17.6 billion+62.4%

Both figures are record highs. The company cited growing demand for next-generation high-speed communications (for AI servers and data centers), a recovery in demand for commodity memory, and strong sales of products for new energy vehicles (NEVs) as growth drivers. Operating profit growing faster than sales can be read as a sign of profit leverage (the effect of fixed costs weighing less as utilization rises). However, this interpretation is an estimate.

2. Full-Year Forecasts Were Also Raised Substantially

  • Full-year operating profit forecast: ¥33.7 billion → ¥38.3 billion (approx. +53% from the previous year)
  • Full-year sales forecast: ¥93.3 billion → ¥101.5 billion
  • Full-year net profit forecast: ¥26.0 billion (approx. +43% from the previous year). It had previously been undecided.

In the previous fiscal year (ended March 2026), sales were about ¥74.5 billion (+3.7%) and operating profit about ¥25.0 billion (-7.2%), a slight decline in profit. In just one year, the picture has shifted from shrinking profit to a forecast of operating profit growth in the 50% range. When Q1 results came out in July, the full-year operating profit forecast was still ¥33.7 billion, and the drop in operating margin from 34.8% to 32.9% was flagged as a concern. This upward revision eases that worry to some extent.

3. What Kind of Company Is MARUWA?

Its business rests on two main pillars.

  • Ceramic components: electronic components, ceramic substrates, and parts for semiconductor manufacturing equipment. Heat-dissipating substrates, which carry heat away efficiently, are used in AI servers and high-speed communications equipment that generate a lot of heat.
  • Lighting equipment: conventional and LED lighting. This segment is relatively small.

As AI chips and servers become more powerful, thermal management becomes more important, and ceramic materials that resist heat and insulate well find wider use. This is why MARUWA draws attention as an AI-related theme stock.

4. How Has the Share Price Moved?

Looking only at confirmed movements, the share price has been quite volatile.

  • It was in the low ¥60,000s in early July this year and again in early October.
  • In early November it came down to around ¥50,000, with a closing price of about ¥50,710 on November 2.
  • In August, a domestic brokerage cut its target price from ¥85,100 to ¥71,700 while keeping a positive rating.

The limit-up came right after the upward revision, but it is worth remembering that the stock had slipped from the ¥60,000s to around ¥50,000 before and after that. One way to see it: the market priced in expectations, partly gave them back, and then got confirmation through earnings. I could not confirm the exact closing price on the date of writing, so please check it directly on your brokerage's quote screen.

5. Shareholders and Dividends

  • The largest shareholder is Kanbe Art, with about 29.5%.
  • Asset managers affiliated with U.S.-based Capital Group (Capital World Investors about 5.7%, Capital Research Global Investors about 5.7%, American Funds SMALLCAP World Fund about 5.6%) and Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management (about 4.4%) are also major shareholders.
  • The annual dividend for the FY ended March 2026 was ¥102, and the dividend forecast for the FY ending March 2027 is ¥110. How this upward revision affects the dividend outlook will need to be checked in further disclosures.

That long-term overseas investors steadily hold shares suggests a relatively solid shareholder base. Korea's National Pension Service does not hold this stock.

6. What to Watch Next

  • Whether H2 targets are met: To reach full-year operating profit of ¥38.3 billion, about ¥20.7 billion is needed in the second half (excluding the ¥17.6 billion in H1). That requires quarterly profit to grow even beyond the first-half level.
  • The AI capex cycle: If customers' data center investment slows, demand could be affected.
  • Margin direction: Even as sales grow, initial costs for new products or rising costs could lower the operating margin.
  • Commodity memory and NEV demand: Both are sensitive to the economy, so it is important to see whether the recovery continues.
  • Volatility: This stock swings enough to hit limit-up, so beware of short-term price fluctuations.

Summary

MARUWA has moved from a year of declining profit to record results and a sharply raised full-year forecast, riding AI and high-speed communications demand. The key questions are whether this pace continues in the second half and how much of the expectation is already priced in. Forecasts are company plans and may differ from actual results.

This article is not investment advice, and investors are responsible for their own investment decisions.
